notes:
Speccify 0.9.3 adds personal Codex workflows, optional Beta updates and a separate local development app.

## Changes

- Connect selected Spec changes to your own local Codex thread from project or workspace settings. Automation starts disabled and requires a separate personal-use confirmation showing each event, its data and the complete command. The first workflows notify on `backlog-next` and `question-answered`.
- Opt into Beta releases in Environment → Updates. Stable remains the default; downloads and installation stay explicit. This regular release does not publish a Beta build.
- Automatically select the only eligible `.agent` source when no selection is saved. Multiple sources still require a choice.
- Recognize the app by its blue-bar icon. Local builds use Speccify Dev with a separate identity, profile, runtime and service ports, so the normal app can remain open during development.

## Update or install

- From published 0.8.8 or later: Environment → Updates → download 0.9.3 → install and restart after resolving the restart checks. Beta opt-in is unnecessary.
- From published 0.8.7 or earlier: install once from https://speccify.io/download/ because those versions use the former private feed.
- Linux deb/rpm: update through your package manager; in-app Linux updates apply to AppImage.

Targets: macOS Apple Silicon, Windows x64, Linux x86_64 and Linux arm64. Windows installers are not Authenticode signed, so SmartScreen may warn; update signatures are verified separately.

## Verification and limits

The release candidate passed Windows/Linux CI and local checks including 332 desktop Rust tests (three ignored), 365 frontend tests, 412 Python tests (one deselected), 27 manifest tests and all ten desktop browser groups. The website build, catalogue and landing checks passed. The broader desktop Clippy check retains 15 existing findings.

Publication requires independent asset/hash checks, four real updater-signature checks and macOS signature, notarization and Gatekeeper verification. See the release guide for the final publication and installed-app update evidence. Windows and Linux interactive installation remain unverified.

Native development checks covered the automation form and confirmation. No real Codex session was notified during verification; fake command runners cover delivery and cancellation. Personal confirmation does not change the applicable service terms. Studio, IDE and navigator organization remain planning topics. A stable build does not prove Beta-suffixed packages or a Beta-to-final update.
